slides.say: Now a very important word, regular. A regular polygon has all its sides equal, and all its angles equal. Both things together.
Here's a regular hexagon. It has six sides, all equal. And it has six angles, all equal. So it looks the same from every direction.
Why do we need both? Look at this. I take two sides of the hexagon and fold them inward. All six sides are still equal. But the angles are not equal any more. So this is not a regular hexagon.
at: the angles are not equal any more

slides.say: It still has six sides, so it's still a hexagon. Its angles still add up to seven hundred twenty. One angle now points inward, and it's bigger than one hundred eighty.
at: it's bigger than one hundred eighty

slides.say: And the other way around. A rectangle has four equal angles, but its sides are not all equal. So a rectangle is not regular. The regular quadrilateral is the square. And the regular triangle is the equilateral triangle.
at: A rectangle has four equal angles
The regular quadrilateral is the square

slides.say: Every regular polygon fits in a circle. We can draw a circle around it, so all its corners are on the circle. The center of that circle, O, is also the center of the polygon.
at: We can draw a circle around it
all its corners are on the circle

slides.say: We can also draw a circle inside it, touching every side. It has the same center, O. But in questions we mostly use the circle around it.
But careful, this works only one way. If a polygon fits in a circle, it's not necessarily regular. Here all the corners are on the circle, but the sides are clearly not equal. So it's not regular.
at: Here all the corners are on the circle

slides.say: Now let's find one angle of a regular polygon. We already know how to find the sum of the angles. In a regular polygon all the angles are equal. So we just divide the sum by the number of angles. And n sides means n angles.
A regular pentagon. The sum is five hundred forty. Five hundred divided by five is one hundred, and forty divided by five is eight. So one angle is one hundred eight.
at: So one angle is one hundred eight

slides.say: A regular hexagon. The sum is seven hundred twenty, divided by six. Six times one hundred twenty is seven hundred twenty. So one angle is one hundred twenty.
at: So one angle is one hundred twenty

slides.say: A regular octagon. The sum is one thousand eighty, divided by eight. Let's halve it three times, because eight is two times two times two. Half is five hundred forty. Half again is two hundred seventy. And half again is one hundred thirty-five.
at: And half again is one hundred thirty-five

slides.say: Remember these three angles, one hundred eight, one hundred twenty and one hundred thirty-five. The exam uses them all the time. And we divide only when the polygon is regular. If it's not regular, the angles are not equal. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
at: we divide only when the polygon is regular
